text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai: Palestinian Authority involved in murders.
- Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu: Israel cannot ignore killing of Arab residents.
- Israeli Attorney-General Elyakim Rubinstein: We can't stop El Al flying on Jewish sabbath.
- World Jewish Restitution Organisation warns European states over Jewish assets.
- Former army chief Ehud Barak considered primary shoo-in.
- Property-tax payments plunge 29 percent so far in 1997. Overall internal revenues increase 1.3 pct in same period.
- Federal Express launches Israel-U.S. route.
- Israel Corporation slips into red.
- Jerusalem's Hechal Shlomo, former seat of Chief Rabbinate, to become theme park.
GLOBES
- Prime minister's office bitterly opposes taxing short-term savings.
- International judicial panel will decide on petitions by Holocaust survivors against Swiss banks.
- National Infrastructure Minister Ariel Sharon leaves on Tuesday for talks in Russia on natural gas.
HAARETZ
- Addition of 400 policemen to enforce law in East Jerusalem.
- Land dealer who was kidnapped and released: "No one is protecting us. We've no security, neither here nor there."
- Finance Minister Dan Meridor: We'll not agree to widen the exchange rate band because it would mean a revaluation.
MAARIV
- Labour chooses a leader. Poll shows Barak winning 55 percent, Yossi Beilin 19 percent, Shlomo Ben-Ami 8 percent, Ephraim Sneh 6 percent.
- Slain Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin's widow Leah: "I am hoping for a new page in the party".
- Berlin opera musician who signed bill in Israel "Adolf Hitler" says there's no limit to his regret.
- Jordanian embassy owes 180,000 shekels rent, owners say.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Labour chooses a chairman.
- Public Security Minister Avigdor Kahalani: The war for Jerusalem is the same as in June 1967.
